newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria invites bids for gas pipeline concessions.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria invites bids for gas pipeline concessions.

text.p: Bulgaria on Friday invited bidders for two pipeline concessions for transiting Russian gas through its territory.

Candidates for a concession on the existing pipelines and for transiting Russian natural gas through them are invited on May 19 at 10 a.m. (0800 GMT) at the Energy Ministry to be present at a competition for chosing a concessionaire, said an announcement of the energy minister published in the State Gazette.

Candidates for a concession for pipelines planned to be built and for transiting Russian natural gas through them are invited on May 21 at 10 a.m. (0800 GMT) at the Energy Ministry, the State Gazette said.
The two concession offers of 35 years each are for six existing transit gas pipelines and for five stretches planned to be built.
The two concessions include existing pipelines to Turkey, Greece and Macedonia and a pipeline to Yugoslavia which is currently being designed.
Bulgaria has 625 km of transit pipelines which receive and transmit gas from outside the country and currently transits Russian gas to Turkey and Greece.
Its pipeline to Macedonia has been constructed and filled with gas but is still waiting for its western neighbours to complete the pipeline on their territory.

The winner of the competition for enlarging the gas transit system on Bulgarian territory, which is expected to cost some $500 million, will operate it under the formula build-operate-transfer, government officials said.
The tender winner should supply Russian gas at preferential prices and part of the volumes should be delivered against Bulgarian goods and services.
The Bulgarian-Russian joint stock company Topenergy, which was set up last year by Gazprom and Bulgargas, is considered as a serious candidate for the concessions.
Gazprom has 50 percent in Topenergy and Bulgargas holds a 25.1 percent stake. The remaining 24.9 percent are distributed among Bulgarian banks and firms.
